text.p: Britain's Trade and Industry ministry said on Tuesday that a ruling on the acquisition by brewery-to-leisure group Bass Plc of Carlsberg-Tetley would be made in the near future.

"I am not able to give a specific date because the information is market-sensitive.The minister is still considering the matter and we expect to announce a ruling in the near future," a ministry spokesman told Reuters.
Bass is seeking to buy Carlsberg's 50 percent share of Carlsberg-Tetley, seen as important in boosting its British business.
The planned deal, which would create Britain's largest brewer and give it a 35 percent market share, is subject to approval by British authorities.
The merger, agreed by Carlsberg and Bass and submitted for regulatory approval last August would leave the Danish brewery group with a 20 percent share in a merged Carlsberg-Tetley-Bass.
Market uncertainty about the sale of Carlsberg-Tetley to Bass and the delay in the deal's clearance by UK regulators has recently caused the Carlsberg share to slip on markets.
The share traded five crowns lower at 380 at 1310 GMT on Tuesday.
